short_description: Pediatric mental health practice offering therapy, psychiatry, psychological testing and parent coaching for kids up to 18, virtually and at New.
long_description: Brightline is a pediatric behavioral health practice for children and teens up to age 18 and their parents. It offers outpatient therapy and psychiatry, diagnostic evaluations, medication management and psychological testing for autism, ADHD, learning differences and executive functioning, with focused programs for anxiety, OCD, ADHD and disruptive behaviour. Families in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut can use its New York-area clinics, video visits or both; families in Massachusetts and Washington can get therapy and psychiatry by video. In California it runs BrightLife Kids, a free state-funded coaching program. Brightline accepts plans including Cigna, Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts and Premera; its published self-pay prices are about $350 for a first therapy session, $200–$275 for ongoing therapy and $225–$350 for psychiatry. The only published study of the service is a 2023 company-funded retrospective study of 703 families, without a control group, in which most children's symptom scores improved.
patient_summary: You start with an in-depth evaluation of your child, then work with a therapist, psychiatrist or coach by video or at a clinic, with parents involved in care. Many employer and insurance plans cover it; without coverage, therapy costs about $200–$275 a session. Kids and teens up to 18 are seen in the states Brightline serves.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; $200–$275/session self-pay ($350 first session)
pricing.notes: Accepts plans including Cigna, Aetna, BCBS of Massachusetts and Premera; often covered by employers. Self-pay psychiatry $225–$350/session; psychological testing $2,000–$5,000. HSA/FSA can be used. Coaching is free for California families through BrightLife Kids.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal information or use cookies for cross-context tracking; clinical records fall under its HIPAA notice, and anyone can request deletion.

seo.title: Brightline: Virtual Mental Health Care for Kids & Teens
seo.meta_description: Brightline provides virtual behavioral health care for children and teens, including therapy, coaching, speech therapy, and psychiatry for ages 1.5-17.

faqs.a: Brightline serves children and teens from 18 months through 17 years old. Different services are appropriate at different ages—early childhood focuses on parent coaching and developmental support, while older children receive individual therapy and psychiatry when needed.

Brightline is typically accessed through employer benefits or health plan partnerships. Check with your HR department to see if your company offers Brightline. If offered, enrollment is usually through the Brightline app or website using your employer credentials.

Yes, Brightline provides comprehensive ADHD evaluation and treatment including behavioral therapy, parent training, executive function coaching, and medication management through child psychiatrists when appropriate.

faqs.q: What makes Brightline different from regular therapy?
faqs.a: Brightline offers a comprehensive care team (therapists, coaches, psychiatrists, speech therapists) rather than standalone therapy. Parents receive coaching alongside child treatment. The platform specializes exclusively in pediatric care, unlike general telehealth platforms.

clinical_trials.study: Retrospective study of Brightline coaching, therapy and psychiatry outcomes

citation.authors: Loo T, Hunt J, Grodberg D, Bravata D
citation.title: Clinical and Psychosocial Outcomes Associated With a Tele-behavioral Health Platform for Families: Retrospective Study

clinical_trials.outcome: 75% of coaching and 69% of therapy/psychiatry participants showed reliable improvement on the PSC-17; funded by Brightline, no control group.

primary_uses: Therapy for child and teen anxiety, OCD and depression

availability.note: Children and teens up to 18. Clinics and video in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut; video only in Massachusetts and Washington; free coaching in California via BrightLife Kids.
